title: Causality as a Corollary of Identity
summary: The law of causality as the law of identity applied to action. A fuller floor than the preview you just climbed.

lessons.title: Identity applied to action
lessons.objective: State the law of causality as the law of identity applied to action, not as a second rule beside identity.

exercises.prompt: On this floor, the law of causality is which of these?

choices.text: The law of identity applied to action
A rival law that replaces identity
A vote about what may happen
A mood about causes

feedback.note: Causality does not sit next to identity as a second primary. It is identity, stated for action.

exercises.prompt: Match each term to the job it does in the law.

pairs.right: A thing is what it is

feedback.note: The base is identity. The corollary carries that base over to what a thing does.

exercises.prompt: Complete the short formula.

parts.text: The law of causality is the law of identity applied to

feedback.note: The word that finishes the formula is action. Voting, mood, and chance are not what identity is applied to here.

exercises.prompt: Build the short formula in order.

feedback.quote: The law of causality is the law of identity applied to action.
feedback.note: The sentence you built is that formula. Chance and against are not part of it.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 152

exercises.prompt: Calling causality a corollary means it is:

choices.text: Identity restated for action, not a later exception
A cancellation of A is A
An optional extra you may skip
A social custom about blame

feedback.note: A corollary here repeats the same fact in a new setting. It does not loosen identity when something acts.

exercises.prompt: Identity is applied to action. Which reading keeps that order?

choices.text: What a thing is comes first; what it does follows from that
What someone wishes comes first and rewrites what it is
Action is settled first and identity is filled in later
Neither identity nor action is involved

feedback.note: Applied to means the same law, moved onto action. It does not mean action gets to ignore what the thing is.

exercises.prompt: Match the phrase to what this floor uses it for.

pairs.right: The move from what a thing is to what it does

feedback.note: Keep the three jobs distinct. The corollary depends on identity. It does not trade places with it.

exercises.prompt: Finish the contrast.

feedback.note: Replace would make causality a rival. Applies keeps it a corollary.

exercises.prompt: The axioms floor already pointed at this dependence. This floor’s job is to:

choices.text: Hold the full statement, not merely a pointer ahead
Drop identity once action begins
Swap causality in as the first axiom
Skip action and stay on names only

feedback.note: The preview named the dependence. This floor stays on it: causality is identity applied to action.

lessons.title: The entities that act
lessons.objective: Locate the cause in the nature of the entities that act, not in a push with no thing behind it.

exercises.prompt: What causes and determines the nature of an action?

choices.text: The nature of the entities that act
Nothing at all
A label stuck on afterward
A crowd’s preference about the entity

feedback.note: The cause is not a loose event floating free of things. It is the nature of the entities that act.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece of the longer clause to its role.

pairs.right: What that nature causes and determines

feedback.note: Entity, nature, and action stay in that order. The action does not assign the entity its nature.

exercises.prompt: Complete the first half of the longer clause.

parts.text: The nature of an action is caused and determined by the nature of the

feedback.note: Entities that act are the cause named here. Wishes and votes are not substitutes for their natures.

exercises.prompt: Build the study line for where the cause sits.

feedback.note: Whim and vote are distractors. The line keeps the cause in the nature of the entity.

exercises.prompt: A supposed cause with no entity behind it is:

choices.text: Not what this law treats as a cause
The best kind of cause
The same fact as an entity’s nature
The only cause identity allows

feedback.note: If nothing acts, there is no nature to determine an action. The law has no room for a cause that is not an entity’s nature.

exercises.prompt: Two actions differ. The first place this law tells you to look is:

choices.text: The natures of the entities that act
Whether the actions were given similar names
Which action a poll prefers
A luck that belongs to neither entity

feedback.note: Different actions point back to different natures. They do not point to a nameless push shared by nothing in particular.

exercises.prompt: Match each story of a cause to the verdict on this floor.

pairs.left: Caused by a wish that the entity be otherwise
pairs.right: Not a cause in this law

feedback.note: Only the entity’s nature is the cause the corollary names. A wish and a blank are not stand-ins for it.

exercises.prompt: Say where the cause is, in study words.

parts.text: There is no cause apart from

feedback.note: What the thing is determines what it does. That is identity applied to action, said from the side of the cause.

exercises.prompt: Which wording is the longer clause on this floor?

choices.text: The nature of an action is caused and determined by the nature of the entities that act
An action is caused by nothing in the entity
An action is caused by the name someone prefers
An action first happens, and a nature is assigned later

feedback.quote: The nature of an action is caused and determined by the nature of the entities that act; a thing cannot act in contradiction to its nature.
feedback.note: The correct choice is the first half of that sentence. The second half is the limit the next lesson holds.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 152

lessons.title: No action against its nature
lessons.objective: Hold that a thing cannot act in contradiction to its nature, while still allowing action that fits what it is.

exercises.prompt: What limit does the corollary put on action?

choices.text: A thing cannot act in contradiction to its nature
A thing can act as any nature one prefers
Actions have no natures
Only names act; entities do not

feedback.quote: The nature of an action is caused and determined by the nature of the entities that act; a thing cannot act in contradiction to its nature.
feedback.note: The limit is the second clause. Action is real. Action against the actor’s nature is not.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 152

exercises.prompt: Match each kind of action to the ruling.

pairs.left: Action in line with what the thing is
Action in contradiction to what the thing is
Action from a thing with no nature
pairs.right: Ruled out, because there is no such actor

feedback.note: The law limits action. It does not ban action. What it bans is action that would contradict the actor.

exercises.prompt: Complete the limit.

feedback.note: Contradiction to its nature is the bar. Favor and title do not name that bar.

exercises.prompt: Build the limit in study words.

feedback.note: May and rename soften or dodge the limit. Cannot act against its nature is the claim.

exercises.prompt: An action that fits what the thing is counts as:

choices.text: Action the law allows, not a contradiction
A contradiction, because all action is banned
A break from identity
A vote that changes its nature

feedback.note: Identity applied to action still leaves the thing able to act. It leaves the thing able to act only as what it is.

exercises.prompt: Cannot, in this law, means:

choices.text: Ruled out by what the thing is, not merely hard or unpopular
Difficult, but open if one tries longer
Illegal under a statute
Rude in company

feedback.note: The bar is metaphysical. It is not a remark about effort, statutes, or manners.

exercises.prompt: Match the phrase to the fact it names.

pairs.right: The action the law rules out
The only actions open to it

feedback.note: The nature sets the limit. Action inside the limit stands. Action outside it does not.

exercises.prompt: Finish the contrast between acting and contradicting.

parts.text: A thing acts as what it

feedback.note: Is names the identity. Contradict names the action the corollary rejects.

exercises.prompt: Which mistake treats the limit as a ban on action itself?

choices.text: Reading cannot contradict its nature as cannot act at all
Reading it as a bar only on contradictory action
Keeping the cause in the entity’s nature
Holding the short formula and the longer clause together

feedback.note: The corollary is about how a thing acts, not about freezing it. Contradictory action is out. Action as such is not.

lessons.title: Not a rival law
lessons.objective: Reject substitutes that treat causality as chance, decree, or a second axiom that can break identity.

exercises.prompt: Which reading is not this law?

choices.text: A decree can make a thing act against its nature
Causality is identity applied to action
The entity’s nature determines the action
Action cannot contradict that nature

feedback.note: A decree is not a cause that rewrites identity. The other three readings are the floor itself.

exercises.prompt: Match each substitute to why it fails.

pairs.right: A cause that is not an entity

pairs.left: A decree that rewrites the entity

pairs.right: A break from identity, which a corollary is not

feedback.note: Each substitute drops the corollary. Chance drops the entity, decree drops the limit, and a rival axiom drops the dependence on identity.

exercises.prompt: Say what causality does not do to identity.

parts.text: identity. It is identity applied to

feedback.note: Break and outrank would make a rival. Action is the setting of the corollary, not a mood.

exercises.prompt: Build the rejection of decree.

feedback.note: Always and vote do not belong. A decree has no power to contradict the actor’s nature.

exercises.prompt: An uncaused action would be:

choices.text: An action with no identity behind it, which the corollary rejects
The ordinary case of identity applied to action
The clearest case of an entity’s nature
What the law of causality requires

feedback.note: If the action had no cause in what the thing is, identity would have failed for action. That is what the corollary rules out.

exercises.prompt: Which trio is outside this law’s subject?

choices.text: Legislation, mood, and a vote about what the entity should be
Identity, the entity’s nature, and its action
The short formula and the limit on contradiction
The nature of the entities that act

feedback.note: The law is about entities in action. It is not a remark on statutes, feelings, or polls.

exercises.prompt: Match the claim to the verdict.

feedback.note: Two denials and two affirmations. The affirmations are the same fact: what the thing is determines what it does.

exercises.prompt: Name the two substitutes this lesson rejects.

feedback.note: Chance and decree are the substitutes. Entity and nature are what the law actually uses.

exercises.prompt: Why is causality not promoted to a first axiom on this floor?

choices.text: Because it depends on identity and only applies identity to action
Because it is older than identity
Because it cancels the need for a nature
Because a vote ranked it first

feedback.note: A corollary cannot outrank the fact it restates. Causality stays downstream of identity.

exercises.prompt: Build the one-line rejection of a rival law.

feedback.note: Replacement would be the rival reading. Not a rival of identity is the reading this floor keeps.

lessons.title: The fuller floor
lessons.objective: Connect the short formula to the longer clause and treat them as one statement, fuller than the preview.

exercises.prompt: The short formula and the longer clause:

choices.text: State one dependence in two wordings
Contradict each other
Belong to two unrelated topics
Are optional slogans with no link

feedback.note: Identity applied to action is the same claim as this: the entity’s nature determines the action, and the action cannot contradict that nature.

exercises.prompt: Match each wording to the part of the floor it carries.

pairs.right: The action’s nature comes from the entities that act
No action in contradiction to that nature

feedback.note: One floor, three wordings of one dependence. Do not file them as separate laws.

exercises.prompt: Tie the formula to the cause.

parts.text: Identity applied to action means the action is

feedback.note: Determined by what the entity is is the bridge between the short formula and the longer clause.

exercises.prompt: Build the short formula once more, as the head of this floor.

feedback.quote: The law of causality is the law of identity applied to action.
feedback.note: Except and sometimes would punch a hole in the corollary. The formula has no such hole.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 152

exercises.prompt: Why is this floor fuller than the preview on the axioms floor?

choices.text: The preview only pointed ahead; this floor states the formula and the clause about nature
This floor drops both sentences and keeps only the pointer
This floor changes the subject away from identity and action
This floor replaces the law with a vote

feedback.note: Fuller means both wordings are in hand: identity applied to action, and the nature of the entities that act.

exercises.prompt: Which order is the dependence?

choices.text: Identity first, then causality as its corollary for action
Causality first, then identity as an optional gloss
Neither depends on the other
A third law comes first and both follow if a decree says so

feedback.note: The order is the point of calling causality a corollary. Identity is not derived from a separate law of causes.

exercises.prompt: Match the question to the answer this floor gives.

pairs.left: What is the law of causality?
pairs.right: The law of identity applied to action
The nature of the entities that act
Action in contradiction to a thing’s nature

feedback.note: Those three answers are the whole floor. If you can give them, you are past the preview.

exercises.prompt: Put the two key phrases in one line.

parts.text: , so a thing cannot act against its

feedback.note: Action and nature are the two words that lock the formula to the limit. Chance and decree are the substitutes already rejected.

exercises.prompt: Leaving this floor, which summary is right?

choices.text: Causality is not a break from identity; a thing acts as what it is
Causality is the break that lets a thing act against what it is
Actions happen, but nothing determines them
Only the preview matters; the two sentences can be dropped

feedback.note: That summary is the unit: the law of identity applied to action, held more fully than the preview that pointed here.
